turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale. My son has a zero in your gradebook for an essay he wrote, and nobody called me before he saw it on his phone in the middle of class. What happened?
Is that meant to be an answer? I asked what happened to Owen's essay, Hale.
WHAT DO YOU WANT FROM ME? I'VE BEEN TEACHING FOR TWENTY YEARS AND EVERY PARENT THINKS THEIR KID IS A GENIUS.
Twenty years, and you still entered a zero before you called his mother. Don't tell me about your experience, Hale. Tell me what you did and why.
Okay. I'm sorry for shouting. Let's be concrete. Tell me your conditions for resolving this, and please number them one, two, three so I can write them on my notepad exactly.

Okay. I won't number them for your notepad, but I'll say them plainly. The zero comes off. Then Owen gets a supervised rewrite, in private, not in front of his class. And nothing about this goes on his record, in writing.

Before any of that, I want to know what you have. What is your evidence that Owen didn't write this essay?
You know, if you keep threatening me with your lawyer voice, I'll file a complaint with the Law Society of Alberta about you using your profession to intimidate a teacher. Is that what you want?
I haven't threatened you, Hale. I asked what evidence you have. File whatever you want with whoever you want. I'm writing down that you're answering a question about the evidence with a complaint.

Fine. On November 2 I talked with Owen for five minutes after class. I asked what epistemological paralysis means; he said 'like, being stuck.' He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. Those notes are from that day. Also, the quote he cites from Act 3, Scene 2 isn't in the play.
That's something I can check. Show me the notes, with the date on them. And if you're saying the quote doesn't exist in the play, I want to see the passage, not your word for it.
I'll pull them up. While I do: did Owen ever talk to you about his argument for this essay, back at the start of October? What did he say Hamlet's problem was?
Hale, I'm not here to tell you what Owen thinks about Hamlet. You're the one who has to show me what Owen wrote and what he said in class. Pull up the notes.
Here are the notes, dated November 2. And here's the thing: there's a real question about when that essay was actually written. Do you know what time Owen finished it?
Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend. If you have a timestamp that says otherwise, show it to me. I'm not going to answer a question about when he finished it from your notes or your memory.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, a supervised rewrite in private, and a written commitment that nothing goes on Owen's record. I expect your answer by Thursday, November 12.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with the zero still standing and no terms accepted.
Moved at: none
